standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: You look a bit shady, if I do say so myself.

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: Well that's the nicest thing anyone has ever said to me!
The name's Oriana. Nice to meet ya!

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.text: Oriana shakes your hand with a strong and aggressive grip. She also tries to get inside your pockets...

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.player: Right... Well I'm [player name]. What is it you do around here?

standard-dialogue-initial-dialogue.npc: Well I'm the best thief to ever live, ain't I.
This place is filled to the brim with wealthy folk with lots of pricey stuff. It's all prime for the takin'.
Now what can I do for you?

options.text: Do you know what these keys are for?
options.condition: If the player has house keys

steps.player: Do you know what these keys are for?

steps.npc: Let me take a look.
Those are keys to the houses round 'ere.

steps.player: Oh, so I can just waltz right in?

steps.npc: Essentially yes! Though the keys you showed me look a bit old. I'd try to find as many as you can just in case they break.

options.text: Can you tell me more about these rich folk?

steps.player: Can you tell me more about these rich folk?

steps.npc: Yes I can. Some 'ave got houses full of loot, while others spend their days at the bazaar. What do you want to know?
Some of them round here are filled with loot for sure. They've got so many bits and bobs, trinkets and doodads, that they 'ardly ever notice they've been robbed.
Oh yes.
First we get keys for these houses, which are always conveniently under the doormat.

steps.player: Are you serious? It's that easy?

steps.npc: Ha... No. I was just pulling your leg.
You'll 'ave to steal the house keys from the citizens.
All these wealthy folk buy and sell property like it's nothing, so they 'ave plenty of spare keys to go round.

steps.player: So how do you steal them?

steps.npc: We pick their pockets of course. I 'ave some of my crew in the bazaar. If you fancy gettin' involved, they might help you out every now and then.
Once you 'ave a key, you can break into a house. Not any ol' house though. It must be one that's ready to be robbed.
The street urchins that roam the streets keep tabs on which houses are vulnerable.
Once you know a house is vulnerable, wait for the owner to leave. Then just simply use your key to get in and steal to your heart's content!
But whatever you do, dont get caught!

steps.player: So... steal keys, use keys on the houses that are ready to be robbed, make buckets of cash and don't be caught?

steps.npc: That's it!
If you're not sure where to begin, chat to the urchins in my crew posted round the houses. They'll help you find the next one to plunder.
Though it might come at a price.
Some of the wealthiest citizens in Varlamore shop in the bazaar and nearby. A perfect place to pick some pockets!

steps.player: Surely it's not so easy though?

steps.npc: You'd be right about that. If it were easy to steal from 'em, they wouldn't be so rich, would they?

steps.player: Sounds like you might have some tips?

steps.npc: Some of the street urchins in my crew hang around in the bazaar and on the outskirts. They might be able to provide some sort of distraction.

steps.player: They do it just out of the goodness of their heart?

steps.npc: You're funny, [player name].
They get a cut in all the wealth we make.
Cheeky! You're lucky I don't steal from you right now!
See you later.
Nah! I 'ave a network of spies and pickpockets that roam the city. You might've seen 'em?

steps.player: Seen them? Not sure I have.

steps.npc: Hidden in plain sight. Perfect! Well it's all the street urchins of course. You can tell if they are part of my crew by the purple sash around their waist.
Most of them lost their parents to the Colosseum, hoping to get glory for their family. The Colosseum 'owever, had other plans...
It really is. They had nowhere to go and no food to eat, so I offered them a home, food, and all the gold they would ever need to 'ave a good life.
No one suspects them, which makes them perfect spies.

steps.player: Can they help me in anyway?

steps.npc: Yes they can! Some in the residential area will point out houses free to rob, and some will be in and around the bazaar, distracting the wealthy citizens.
It sure is, but give them any trouble, and I'll throw you in the Colosseum myself.
Not much to tell really.
I was an orphan, much like these street urchins you see around the city. I spent my days running around scrounging for food and struggling to find somewhere to sleep.
Eventually, I turned to a life of crime and thievery. Turns out I'm quite good at it.
I took refuge in a small spot in the north east of the city. Out of sight, out of mind.
There I met with other orphans just like me. We all wanted payback. Payback on the city for forgetting about us.

steps.player: I'm sure there are better places for you and your crew to find refuge outside of the city. Even outside of Varlamore.

steps.npc: That may be the case, [player name], but I can't in good conscience leave any of the folk here who are struggling. I swore to help anyone in need.
While the Colosseum still stands, family greed for glory will cost people. Some just their livelihoods, others their lives!

steps.player: So you really want to make a difference?

steps.npc: Well don't get me wrong, I still want to get filthy stinking rich as well!
See you later.

standard-dialogue-after-stealing-valuabl.player: I have actually! I've found these valuables from some of the houses.

standard-dialogue-after-stealing-valuabl.npc: Want some coin for those? I'll give you a good deal... One coin a piece.

standard-dialogue-after-stealing-valuabl.player: One measly coin? That hardly seems worth it.

standard-dialogue-after-stealing-valuabl.npc: The thing is, you won't be able to sell those yourself, making them worthless. Still, how 'bout five coins a piece?
That's crazy! Ever 'eard of inflation. It affects us thieves too...

standard-dialogue-after-stealing-valuabl.text: If the player has not reached Gladiator rank in the Fortis Colosseum:

steps.npc: 55 coins is my final offer.

standard-dialogue-after-stealing-valuabl.text: If the player has reached Gladiator rank in the Fortis Colosseum:

steps.npc: 65 coins is my final offer. I've even throw in a little extra as you seem to be the talk of the town, [rank].

standard-dialogue-after-stealing-valuabl.player: I suppose that's better than nothing.

standard-dialogue-after-stealing-valuabl.npc: Good. Do you want to trade them in now?

steps.text: How many valuables would you like to hand in?
You hand in [number] valuable items for [number] coins.

steps.npc: There ya go! Don't spend it all at once.
Suit yourself. What to chat 'bout something else?

standard-dialogue-if-trading-valuables-t.text: How many valuables would you like to hand in?
You hand in [number] valuable items for [number] coins.

standard-dialogue-if-trading-valuables-t.npc: There ya go! Don't spend it all at once.

standard-dialogue-if-trading-in-nothing-.npc: You don't seem to anything to trade in to me.

standard-dialogue-if-trading-in-nothing-.text: You need some valuables  from nearby houses to trade in.
